newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-CROOKES HELPS NATAL TO CRUSHING WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CROOKES HELPS NATAL TO CRUSHING WIN.

text.p: A return of 5-43 from off-spinner
Derek Crookes helped Natal to a crushing victory by an innings
and 156 runs over Griqualand West on the third day of their
four-day Supersport Series cricket match at Kingsmead on Monday.
Natal, with their fourth win in six games, moved to the top
of the Supersport Series table by three points as Griquas were
bowled out for 166 in their second innings on the penultimate
day.
Crookes, who top-scored with an unbeaten 128 in Natal's
first innings, was made man of the match as his side outclassed
Griquas with more than four and a half sessions of the game
remaining.
His five-wicket haul was his sixth in first-class cricket.
Resuming on their overnight score of 19 for one, Griquas
were bowled out in just 62.2 overs, with the only real batting
reistance coming from Cedric English (41), Pieter Barnard (33)
and Ralph Koster (30).
English and Barnard combined in the one substantial
partnership of the innings as they added 63 for the fourth
wicket before Barnard top-edged a pull to Dale Benkenstein
moving in from mid wicket.
"We won our last match in three days at St Georges Park,
which gave us another sniff at the championship, and it's great
to win in three days here at Kingmead," Natal captain Dale
Benkenstein said after his team's victory.
"Playing against a side like Griquas, you can be a little
bit apprehensive as it's often the underdogs who are the guys
who come up trumps. But it's good to be expected to win -- and
then to finish the way we did today."
